blocks.title: Why do precedents usually show higher multiples?
blocks.teaser: Buyers pay a control premium to take control of the company's cash flows and strategy.
blocks.body:
Buyers pay a control premium to take control of the company's cash flows and strategy. Strategic buyers may also pay for synergies.

**Interview answer:** "Acquirers pay for control — and sometimes synergies — so deal multiples run above trading multiples."

blocks.prompt: Why do precedent transaction multiples usually exceed trading multiples?

options.text: Buyers pay a control premium, and strategics may pay for synergies
Private companies always trade at a premium

blocks.explanation: Acquirers pay for control (typically a 20–40% premium) and sometimes synergies, which pushes deal multiples above trading multiples.

blocks.title: Strategic vs. financial buyers — who pays more?
blocks.teaser: Strategic buyers usually, because they can realize synergies (cost cuts, cross-selling) and have a lower cost of capital.
blocks.body: Strategic buyers usually, because they can realize synergies (cost cuts, cross-selling) and have a lower cost of capital. Financial buyers are limited by return targets, though in strong credit markets sponsors can compete aggressively.

blocks.title: Why are old deals less useful?
blocks.teaser: Interest rates, credit availability, and market multiples change.
blocks.body: Interest rates, credit availability, and market multiples change. A deal from a zero-rate era can overstate what a buyer would pay today.

blocks.title: What's a premiums-paid analysis?
blocks.teaser: For public targets, look at the premium buyers paid over the pre-announcement share price in comparable deals, then apply that range to the target's…
blocks.body: For public targets, look at the premium buyers paid over the pre-announcement share price in comparable deals, then apply that range to the target's current price.
